questions.q: Match each utility to what it does.
pairs: Scrambles files so they cannot be read without the key
Moves the parts of files together so they are read faster
Makes files smaller so they take less space to store or send
Keeps a second copy of files in case the first is lost
questions.feedback: Four utilities, four different jobs. None of them is part of the operating system's own management work.

questions.q: Explain why defragmenting a magnetic hard disk makes it faster to read files, but does nothing for a solid state drive.

markPoints.concept: on a hard disk a fragmented file is spread across the platters
markPoints.exemplar: On a hard disk the parts of a file end up scattered across the platters.

markPoints.concept: so the read/write head has to move further and the read takes longer
markPoints.exemplar: The read/write head has to move further, so reading the file takes longer.

markPoints.concept: a solid state drive has no moving parts, so where the data sits makes no difference
accept: no moving parts|nothing moves|no head|no platter|solid state
markPoints.exemplar: An SSD has no moving parts, so it makes no difference where the data is.

questions.example: On a magnetic hard disk the parts of a file become scattered across the platters, so the read/write head has to move between them and reading the file takes longer. Putting the parts back together means less head movement. A solid state drive has no moving parts at all, so every location takes the same time to reach and defragmenting it achieves nothing — while wearing the drive out slightly.
questions.paraphrase: A file on a magnetic drive gets split across the disc, and because the arm must travel between the pieces, reading it is slower; gathering them together reduces that movement. On a solid state drive nothing moves, so the position of the data is irrelevant.
questions.feedback: Three ideas, and the third is the one that shows you understand why the first two matter.
questions.hint: What physically has to happen on a hard disk that does not happen on an SSD?
